# Attaching a Ref to the Input

#### Course: React Hooks: Level Up Your First Web App

## Attaching a Ref to the Input

First, let's create a ref and attach it to the input element. This gives us a stable handle to the DOM node across all re-renders.

```undefined
1import { useState, useEffect } from "react";
2import Header from "./components/Header";
3import EntryCard from "./components/EntryCard";
4
5function App() {
6  const [entries, setEntries] = useState([]);
7  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
8  const [error, setError] = useState(null);
9  const [refreshKey, setRefreshKey] = useState(0);
10
11  useEffect(function () {
12    async function loadEntries() {
13      try {
14        const res = await fetch("https://api.programiz.pro/api/Demo/v1/journal-entries");
15        if (!res.ok) {
16          throw new Error("Could not load entries. Status: " + res.status);
17        }
18        const data = await res.json();
19        const mapped = data.map((post) => {
20          return {
21            ...post,
22            date: new Date(post.date).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
23              year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric"
24            }).toUpperCase()
25          };
26        });
27        setEntries(mapped);
28        setIsLoading(false);
29      } catch (err) {
30        setError(err.message);
31        setIsLoading(false);
32      }
33    }
34    loadEntries();
35  }, [refreshKey]);
36
37  return (
38    <div className="main-container">
39      <Header />
40      <section className="entries-section">
41        <div className="entry-list-header">
42          <h3>Recent Entries</h3>
43          <span className="entry-count">{entries.length}</span>
44          <button
45            className="btn btn-secondary"
46            onClick={() => setRefreshKey((k) => k + 1)}
47          >
48            Refresh
49          </button>
50        </div>
51        {isLoading ? (
52          <p className="loading-state">Loading entries...</p>
53        ) : error ? (
54          <div className="error-banner">
55            <p className="error-label">Something went wrong.</p>
56            <p className="error-detail">{error}</p>
57          </div>
58        ) : entries.length === 0 ? (
59          <p className="empty-state">No entries found.</p>
60        ) : (
61          entries.map((entry) => (
62            <EntryCard
63              key={entry.id}
64              id={entry.id}
65              title={entry.title}
66              date={entry.date}
67              content={entry.content}
68              author={entry.author}
69            />
70          ))
71        )}
72      </section>
73    </div>
74  );
75}
76
77export default App;
```

```undefined
1import { useState, useRef } from "react";
2
3function Header() {
4  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
5
6  // Create the ref
7  const searchRef = useRef(null);
8
9  return (
10    <header className="header">
11      ... ... ...
12      {/* Attach the ref to input element */}
13      <input
14        ref={searchRef}
15        className="search-input"
16        type="text"
17        placeholder="Search entries..."
18        value={query}
19        onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
20      />
21    </header>
22  );
23}
```

```undefined
1function EntryCard({ id, title, date, author, content }) {
2  return (
3    <div className="entry-card">
4      <p className="entry-date">{date}</p>
5      <h2 className="entry-title">{title}</h2>
6      <p className="entry-author">by {author}</p>
7      <p className="entry-content">{content}</p>
8    </div>
9  );
10}
11
12export default EntryCard;
```


After the first render, searchRef.current points to the actual <input> DOM node. Now you can call .focus() on it.
